advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the two-consecutive-hour alarm still fires under GitHub scheduler jitter/dropped runs (missing hourly datapoint + notBreaching breaks the streak); consider a wider evaluation window or documenting the reduced robustness.
evidence: reconcile-bridge.yml comment: 'GitHub's scheduler is best-effort and ... an on-:00 entry is the likeliest to be delayed or dropped' — a dropped hourly run leaves that 3600s bucket with missing data, which notBreaching scores as not-breaching and breaks the two-consecutive-period streak
.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:402 metric is published only per-run ('1 on failure, 0 on success'), so a hour with no run at all publishes no datapoint
advisory.finding: The retuned bridge_run_failures alarm (evaluation_periods=2, datapoints_to_alarm=2, threshold=0, treat_missing_data=notBreaching) requires two CONSECUTIVE hourly buckets to each contain a breaching datapoint; because the bridge now fires only once an hour and GitHub's scheduler is best-effort (runs delayed/dropped, as the change itself relies on for the off-:00 choice), a sustained outage in which the second hour's run is dropped/delayed out of its bucket produces missing data that notBreaching treats as non-breaching, breaking the streak and suppressing the page. The old sub-hourly form had two chances per hour, so this narrows detection robustness in a way the rationale does not acknowledge.
scenarios: Token/credential outage persists across hours but the runner pool is contended enough that one of the two hourly bridge runs is dropped or slips into an adjacent 3600s bucket, so no two consecutive buckets both breach and the alarm never fires.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the two-consecutive-datapoints alarm still pages on a sustained outage when a best-effort scheduled hourly run is dropped/delayed (consider datapoints_to_alarm=2 over evaluation_periods=3, or M-of-N, to tolerate one missing bucket).
evidence: docs/jira-sync-setup.md:201: `GitHub's `schedule` trigger has a 5-minute floor and is best-effort (runs are delayed/dropped under load).`
.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:45-46: `GitHub's scheduler is best-effort and most heavily contended at :00, so an on-:00 entry is the likeliest to be delayed or dropped.`
ABSENCE: nothing in the alarm config compensates for a dropped/absent hourly datapoint breaking the required consecutive-streak; a single missing bucket resets the alarm to OK.
advisory.finding: The retuned bridge_run_failures alarm requires two CONSECUTIVE breaching hourly datapoints (evaluation_periods=2, datapoints_to_alarm=2) combined with treat_missing_data="notBreaching", but the bridge's schedule trigger is best-effort (runs are delayed/dropped under load, per the workflow's own comments and docs). A dropped or slot-delayed run publishes no datapoint for that hour; that missing bucket is treated as not-breaching and breaks the two-consecutive streak, so a sustained credential/token outage that coincides with even one missing hourly run can silently fail to page — reintroducing the exact silent-monitoring gap this metric exists to catch. The prior single-datapoint design (evaluation_periods=1/threshold=1) did not depend on two adjacent buckets both being present.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use an M-of-N evaluation (e.g. evaluation_periods = 3, datapoints_to_alarm = 2) so a single dropped/delayed hourly run does not reset the sustained-failure signal, while a lone blip still stays quiet.
